## VST Investment Thesis — May 2026

### The Setup: AI Electricity Demand Meets Nuclear Renaissance
Vistra Corp owns the largest independent power fleet in the US — ~41 GW of nuclear, natural gas, coal, solar and battery storage across competitive electricity markets, primarily ERCOT (Texas) and PJM (Midwest/Mid-Atlantic). Following the 2024 acquisition of Energy Harbor's nuclear fleet (Perry, Beaver Valley — 4 reactors, ~4GW), Vistra is now one of the largest nuclear operators in the country. This matters enormously because AI data centers need 24/7 reliable, carbon-free baseload power that only nuclear and dispatchable gas can provide — renewable solar/wind cannot meet this requirement without multi-day battery backup.

### Earnings Volatility Is the Key Complexity
The stock confuses investors because GAAP earnings are highly volatile: -$1.2B in FY2022 (gas price spike), +$1.5B in FY2023, +$2.7B in FY2024, and back to +$0.9B TTM. This is not business model deterioration — it is wholesale electricity price cyclicality. The mechanism: VST generates and sells power in deregulated markets where prices are set by the marginal cost of the last generator dispatched (usually natural gas). In a mild/low-demand year, prices are depressed. In a tight-supply year (heat waves, cold snaps, AI demand growth), prices spike dramatically. VST's improved hedging program since FY2022 has reduced tail risk but cannot eliminate commodity exposure.

### The Share Count Trap
VST has 338.6M basic shares outstanding but 424.4M fully diluted — a 25.4% gap from ~85.8M warrants issued when the company emerged from the Energy Future Holdings bankruptcy in 2016. Screeners and quick analyses using basic shares overstate EPS by 25%. Our DCF uses the diluted count throughout; the 'real' forward EPS on a diluted basis is ~$9 (FY2026 analyst consensus), not the $11.21 implied by the forward P/E calculation (which appears to use basic shares).

### Valuation: Below Fair Value Despite +952% Five-Year Run
At $155.28, VST trades at just 13.9x forward P/E (using basic shares) or ~17x on diluted basis — modest for a business with credible double-digit EPS growth ahead. Our DCF yields a base case fair value of $149 and probability-weighted value of $196 (+26.5%). The analyst consensus is more bullish at $230 (19 analysts, Strong Buy). The gap between our base case ($149) and the current price is narrow — this is primarily a bull case story where the AI/nuclear PPA repricing drives earnings well beyond analyst FY2026/FY2027 projections.

### The Constella Energy Angle
VST has discussed a potential spinoff of its nuclear assets (tentatively 'Constella Energy') to unlock a pure-play nuclear premium multiple. Constellation Energy (CEG) — the closest comparable — trades at 30x+ P/E on its nuclear portfolio. If VST's 4GW nuclear fleet is spun off and re-rated at a similar multiple, the implied value is substantial. This is not in our base case but drives the bull scenario materially.

Bear margin 6% ≈ TTM 5.32% + modest recovery. Bull margin 20% = above FY2024 peak (15.44%) justified by premium AI PPA pricing.

The +31% Y1 spike is driven by: (a) Energy Harbor nuclear fleet first full integration year, (b) ERCOT/PJM wholesale power price recovery from depressed TTM levels, (c) new PPA contracts beginning contribution. This is structurally a one-time uplift, not a sustainable 5yr growth rate. Trajectory modelling: Y1 +31%, Y2 +7%, Y3-Y5 +5% → Y5 revenue $28,848M → 5yr CAGR = 10.2% (rounded to 10% base). Deviation from blended 19.1% = -9.1pp — explicitly justified as structural (one-time integration year). Bear 4% = utility mature-phase growth only. Bull 18% ≈ blended consensus, assuming elevated power prices sustained throughout.

Net margin typical 15-25% (regulated), bear trough variable (commodity-exposed). Applied: bear exitPE 12 (conservative floor), base exitPE 20 (growth ceiling, justified by AI/nuclear premium), bull exitPE 28 (between Utilities growth 20 and Energy Renewables median 35 — VST re-rating as AI infrastructure, explicitly justified). Note: VST is NOT a regulated utility — it is deregulated, commodity-exposed, and has higher earnings volatility than the Utilities benchmark implies.

TTM net income dropped sharply from $2,659M (FY2024) to $944M (TTM) — 64.5% decline. EPS fell from $7.26 to $2.22. This appears to be commodity price timing (ERCOT spot price cyclicality) and possibly hedging program timing, NOT structural deterioration. Analyst recovery to $9.00 EPS in FY2026 confirms this view.

FY2022 net margin -8.94% ($-1,227M NI) was driven by the 2022 natural gas price spike catching VST under-hedged. Under the improved hedging program post-FY2022, a repeat is less likely but cannot be ruled out in an extreme commodity scenario.

Analyst Y1 revenue range is extraordinarily wide: $18.8B to $27.5B (range = $8.7B on a $17.7B base). This reflects fundamental uncertainty around ERCOT/PJM spot prices, PPA volume ramp timing, and AI demand acceleration. Standard ±3pp growth anchoring is inappropriate for such a wide-range commodity business; trajectory-derived CAGR was used instead.
